name: weclapp Cloud ERP
description: Access weclapp Cloud ERP data including parties (customers/suppliers), sales orders, invoices, and articles. Popular ERP for German SMBs.
instructions:
weclapp is a cloud ERP for small and mid-sized companies. This connector reads parties (customers, suppliers, contacts), sales orders, sales invoices, recurring invoices, quotations, articles and opportunities through the weclapp REST API v2. Every tool is read-only.

**Getting credentials**
1. In weclapp, open your user menu → **My settings** → **API** and copy the API token into `WECLAPP_API_TOKEN`. Each user has one token; generating a new one invalidates the old one.
2. Set `WECLAPP_TENANT` to the first part of your weclapp address only: for `acme.weclapp.com`, enter `acme`. Requests go to `https://acme.weclapp.com/webapp/api/v2` with the token in the `AuthenticationToken` header.

**Permissions follow the user**: the token acts as the weclapp user it belongs to, so records that user's role cannot see are missing from the results. Use a user with read access to sales, CRM and articles.

**Finding records**: get tools take the internal id, a numeric string such as `"3346"`, not the document number. To find a document by its number, filter the list tool: `orderNumber-eq=SO-1042`, `invoiceNumber-eq=RE-1042`, `quotationNumber-eq=AN-1042`, `articleNumber-eq=A5101`. Customers and suppliers both live under `/party`: filter with `customer-eq=true` or `supplier-eq=true`.

**Filter syntax**: `filter` is sent as query parameters written `property-operator=value` and joined with `&`, e.g. `paymentStatus-eq=OPEN&dueDate-lt=1767225600000`. Operators: `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `gt`, `le`, `ge`, `like`, `ilike`, `in`, `notin`, `null`, `notnull`. `-null` and `-notnull` take an empty value (`customerNumber-notnull=`); `-in` takes a bracketed list. A property name that does not exist returns HTTP 400, in `filter` and in `properties` alike. Sales documents have no `customerName`: the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`.

**Data formats**: dates are Unix epoch milliseconds, in responses and in filters (2026-01-01 00:00 UTC is `1767225600000`). Prices and quantities come back as decimal strings such as `"119.00"`. Unpaid invoices are `paymentStatus-eq=OPEN`, cancelled ones `status-eq=CANCELLED`, credit notes `salesInvoiceType-eq=CREDIT_NOTE`: leave credit notes out when adding up revenue.

**Pagination and limits**: `page` starts at 1; `pageSize` defaults to 100 and is capped at 1000. Fetch the next page until a page returns fewer rows than `pageSize`, and pass only the fields you need in `properties` on large lists. weclapp has no fixed rate limit, but it queues requests under heavy load and answers HTTP 429 after 30 seconds in the queue: wait, then retry.

**Recurring invoices**: `/recurringInvoice` is not part of weclapp's published OpenAPI file. If `weclapp_list_recurring_invoices` returns 404 on a tenant, the resource is not available there; invoices generated from a recurring invoice still carry its `recurringInvoiceId`.

**Cloud reachability**: `*.weclapp.com` is publicly reachable over HTTPS.

WECLAPP_TENANT.help: The first part of your weclapp address: acme for acme.weclapp.com. Not the whole address.

tools.name: weclapp_list_customers
tools.description: List parties (customers/suppliers/contacts) from weclapp ERP. In API v2 customers and suppliers are unified under /party — pass filter='customerNumber-notnull=' to restrict to customers, or filter='supplierNumber-notnull=' for suppliers (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value — NOT '=true'). Use `properties` to limit returned fields (e.g. 'id,customerNumber,company,firstName,lastName,email') to reduce payload size.

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return, e.g. 'id,customerNumber,company,firstName,lastName,email'

filter.description: weclapp v2 filter expression. The property+operator IS the param name (no 'filter=' wrapper). Examples: 'partyType-eq=ORGANIZATION', 'customerNumber-notnull=' — note the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, not '=true'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending (e.g. '-createdDate')

tools.name: weclapp_get_customer
tools.description: Get a specific party (customer/supplier/contact) by ID. In API v2 this maps to /party/id/{id}.

tools.name: weclapp_list_sales_orders
tools.description: List sales orders from weclapp ERP. Returns order numbers, amounts, status and the record address. NOTE: salesOrder has NO 'customerName' field — do not request it in `properties` (weclapp returns 400). The customer's name is in `recordAddress`; the customer link is `customerId`. Use `properties` to limit fields and `filter` to narrow results (e.g. 'orderNumber-eq=SO-1042'). Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds (e.g. 'orderDate-gt=1767225600000').

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

tools.name: weclapp_list_invoices
tools.description: List sales invoices from weclapp ERP. Returns invoice numbers, amounts, due dates, and payment status. NOTE: invoice has NO 'customerName' field — do not request it in `properties` (weclapp returns 400); the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`. Other common 400 traps: line items are `salesInvoiceItems` (not `invoiceItems`); the invoice-type field/filter is `salesInvoiceType` (not `invoiceType`); there is no `currencyName` (currency is `recordCurrencyId`, amounts are `netAmount`/`grossAmount`/`netAmountInCompanyCurrency`); a cancelled invoice is `status-eq=CANCELLED`, not an invoiceType. Use `filter` for queries like 'paid-eq=false'. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds (e.g. 'invoiceDate-gt=1767225600000' for 2026-01-01).

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

filter.description: weclapp filter. The property+operator IS the param name, so pass it as `property-operator=value` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, e.g. 'articleNumber-notnull='). The -in/-notin operators need a BRACKETED comma list: 'id-in=[6501,84566]' — NOT 'id-in=6501,84566' (that returns 400 'invalid parameter value'). Examples: 'articleNumber-eq=A5101', 'productionArticle-eq=true', 'name-ilike=%hammer%'. Combine with '&'.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending

tools.name: weclapp_list_articles
tools.description: List articles (products) from weclapp ERP. Returns article numbers, names, and stock info. Use `filter` like 'articleNumber-eq=ABC123' for SKU lookups. NOTE on prices: an article has NO direct `salesPrice`/`purchasePrice`/`lastPurchasePrice`/`averagePurchasePrice`/`valuationPrice` property (those return 400 'unknown property'). Sales prices live in the `articlePrices` sub-entity and purchase prices in `supplySources` (note: `supplySources`, not `articleSupplySources`) — request those names in `properties` to get the nested price objects.

properties.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return

filter.description: weclapp filter. The property+operator IS the param name, so pass it as `property-operator=value` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, e.g. 'articleNumber-notnull='). The -in/-notin operators need a BRACKETED comma list: 'id-in=[6501,84566]' — NOT 'id-in=6501,84566' (that returns 400 'invalid parameter value'). Examples: 'articleNumber-eq=A5101', 'productionArticle-eq=true', 'name-ilike=%hammer%'. Combine with '&'.

tools.name: weclapp_list_quotations
tools.description: List sales quotations (Angebote) from weclapp ERP. Returns quotation numbers, amounts, status and the record address. NOTE: a quotation has NO 'customerName' field — the customer's name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`; do not request 'customerName' in `properties`. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds (e.g. 'quotationDate-gt=1767225600000' for 2026-01-01).

properties.description: Comma-separated weclapp field names to limit the response (omit to return all fields). Use real field names only — requesting a non-existent property returns a 400.

filter.description: weclapp filter. The property+operator IS the param name, so pass it as `property-operator=value` (NOT a `filter=` wrapper). Operators: -eq -ne -gt -lt -ge -le -like -ilike -in -notin -null -notnull (the -null/-notnull operators take an EMPTY value, e.g. 'quotationNumber-notnull='). Examples: 'status-eq=ORDER_CONFIRMATION_PRINTED', 'quotationNumber-eq=AN-1042'. Combine with '&'.

Returns interval, next run, amounts and status. NOTE: no 'customerName' field — the name is in `recordAddress`, the link is `customerId`. Date fields are Unix epoch milliseconds.
